name: El Segundo Buildworks
status: Independent PointCast studio concept and open production notebook
disclosure: Original design concepts and illustrative planning tools. No physical inventory, tested prototypes, operating workshop, manufacturing capacity, team, student cohort or supplier partnership is claimed. Nothing is available to order here.

concepts.name: Jetty Arc
concepts.size: Proposed 28 × 24 mm; thickness and clutch to quote
concepts.story: A cobalt horizon held inside an open arc. A pocket-sized memory of wave sets and the meeting of coast and infrastructure.
concepts.material: Proposed plated base metal with two enamel colors. Base alloy and finish declarations required.
concepts.question: Can two large color fields stay legible at pin scale, without fragile bridges?
concepts.qc: Check scaled artwork, minimum metal bridges, enamel fill, plating consistency, front/back edges, pin post placement and clutch retention. Agree tolerances with the maker before sample approval.

concepts.name: Blue Hour
concepts.story: An original coastal grid: sunset circle, hangar-like blocks and a low blue horizon. El Segundo’s working landscape translated into shapes, with no copied building logo or civic seal.
concepts.material: Paper label for indoor packaging, or durable film for a surface-use version. These have different end-of-life paths.
concepts.question: Does the composition read at arm’s length and after a small edge scuff?
concepts.qc: Check CMYK proof, bleed and cut line, adhesive/substrate suitability, corner lift, rub resistance and removal residue on the intended surface. Outdoor life is unverified until tested.

concepts.name: Tide Window
concepts.story: Three tide bands cross a yellow window. A quiet graphic reminder that the same stretch of water keeps changing.
concepts.material: Proposed printed flexible magnetic sheet. No detachable high-powered magnet is proposed; product-specific safety review still required.
concepts.question: Will the graphic and backing survive handling on the chosen steel surface?
concepts.qc: Check dimensions, flatness, backing adhesion, edge damage, print wear and holding performance on intended substrates. Keep magnets from children and inspect any separation; sheet format is not a safety certification.

concepts.name: Civic Canopy
concepts.size: Proposed 80 × 85 mm; 3 mm wood as quote starting point
concepts.story: A sculptural tree crown over a simple sidewalk. A civic shape for a room, a seasonal display or a gift wrap, drawn from the feeling of Main Street shade.
concepts.material: Proposed responsibly sourced plywood with water-based print if validated. Cord, ink, adhesive and finish need documented specifications.
concepts.question: Can the hanging hole and grain orientation resist repeated handling?
concepts.qc: Inspect splinters, cut edges, hole strength, cord attachment, print alignment and coating transfer. Agree wood variation range. Keep cords and small parts away from young children; not a toy.

concepts.name: Shift Token
concepts.size: Proposed 35 mm diameter with an integral hole
concepts.story: A sun and a stepped horizon mark the end of a workday. An abstract keepsake for a key ring or desk, with no denomination, currency claim or industrial certification.
concepts.material: Proposed stamped aluminum or brass. Alloy, plating, surface finish, skin contact and attachment suitability to verify.
concepts.question: Does the relief stay readable while the edges remain comfortable?
concepts.qc: Check burrs, edges, hole geometry, surface staining, coating adhesion and key-ring wear. Request approved finishing and material declarations; final process and tooling remain quote-dependent.

concepts.name: Common Elements
concepts.size: Proposed 90 × 55 mm tags and folded bands; dieline to confirm
concepts.story: A small alphabet of waves, grids and warm circles: hang tags, backing cards, bands and color chips that let the object family speak in one voice.
concepts.material: Proposed uncoated paper with one or two inks. Elements means materials and components, not chemical fabrication.
concepts.question: Can one paper size serve a pin, an ornament and a short care note?
concepts.qc: Check trim, fold/crease, stock grain, ink rub, barcode readability if used and pack count. Test attachment and shipping fit. Confirm paper sourcing and local disposal instructions before claims.

finishes.name: Soft enamel
finishes.feel: Raised metal lines; color sits lower
finishes.best: Simple bold pin or medallion shapes
finishes.tradeoff: A die/mold and separated color cells make tooling relevant. Recesses change the tactile finish; fine lines and small bridges need maker review.
finishes.proof: Vector metal boundaries, color references, plating, back/post placement and physical sample
finishes.endOfLife: Mixed metal, enamel and attachment; plan long use, not a blanket curbside recycling claim.

finishes.name: Hard enamel
finishes.tradeoff: Filling and polishing add process steps. Color/plating limits and unit cost are supplier-specific; do not assume every soft-enamel design transfers unchanged.
finishes.proof: Color cells, polishing detail, plating compatibility and approved sample
finishes.endOfLife: A small composite keepsake; preserve material evidence and repair/attachment options.

finishes.name: Printed metal / relief
finishes.feel: Flat printed detail or shallow relief
finishes.best: Gradients, fine image detail or a spare token
finishes.tradeoff: Print can carry detail without many enamel cells. Protective coating, exposed edges, relief tooling and wear differ; stamping and printing are separate quote paths.
finishes.proof: Substrate/alloy, print or relief artwork, protective finish and rub/wear test
finishes.endOfLife: Coatings and mixed attachments complicate recovery. Identify materials rather than promising recyclability.

finishes.name: Printed sticker
finishes.best: Low-risk art sampling and packaging graphics
finishes.tradeoff: Paper is useful indoors; film may tolerate more exposure but adhesive and liner create waste. Confirm exact substrate and intended surface.
finishes.proof: Scaled CMYK artwork, supplier bleed/cut line and adhesive trial
finishes.endOfLife: Ask about liner and adhesive waste. A paper face alone does not make the entire sticker recyclable.

finishes.name: Flexible magnet print
finishes.best: A graphic for a fridge or steel cabinet
finishes.tradeoff: Requires backing/print bonding and a defined holding task. Avoid detached high-powered components; no magnet format is automatically child-safe.
finishes.proof: Thickness, substrate compatibility, edge/peel checks and safety classification
finishes.endOfLife: Usually a composite. Durable use and restrained packaging are safer claims than universal recycling.

finishes.name: Printed wood ornament
finishes.best: Seasonal keepsakes with a hanging point
finishes.tradeoff: Grain, edge color and print can vary. Hole strength, splinters, cord and coatings need sample inspection; quote assembled and unassembled options.
finishes.proof: Scaled outline, hole clearance, grain/print tolerance and cord attachment
finishes.endOfLife: Coatings, glue and cord matter. Verify source claims and avoid assuming compostability.

finishes.name: Paper + card
finishes.best: Backing cards, bands, tags and element kits
finishes.tradeoff: Low tooling for standard sizes; custom dies and finishing add cost. Match stock, crease and ink to handling and shipping needs.
finishes.proof: Dieline, trim/bleed, grain direction, fold dummy and printed sample
finishes.endOfLife: Simple unlaminated designs can reduce material complexity; local collection rules and inks still matter.

finishes.name: Embroidered patch
finishes.best: A textile translation of a bold motif
finishes.tradeoff: Stitch density, thread changes and backing affect quote and stiffness. Tiny type and gradients become thread decisions; requires a redesigned sample, not just a pin file.
finishes.proof: Digitized stitch proof, border, backing, thread colors and sew/adhesion trial
finishes.endOfLife: Mixed fibers, backing and adhesive. Specify composition and attachment before making care claims.

sources.title: Enamel pin reference prices
sources.summary: Public table: 100 one-inch soft-enamel pins at US$3.00 each ($300 reference subtotal); hard enamel US$3.09 each ($309). Advertises no minimum and about 20 days production after artwork approval.
sources.limit: Reference pricing only. Calendar vs business days is unspecified. Artwork, plating, backing, packaging and shipping change the quote; tooling, taxes and freight require confirmation.

sources.title: Enamel and printed pin options
sources.summary: GS-JJ describes recessed soft enamel, polished hard enamel and printed detail/gradients. States minimum one piece with a fixed mold fee. Published examples: 2–7 business days enamel, 4–6 UV print, plus 3–5 business days shipping.
sources.limit: Promotional starting prices are not comparable selected configurations. Exact artwork, mold fee, finish and sample approval may change cost and timing; these are supplier claims, not commitments.

sources.title: Die-cut sticker pilot
sources.summary: Published minimum 10 stickers, online proofs/revisions and four-day turnaround. Die cutting cuts both sticker and backing to the outline; kiss cutting retains a larger backing.
sources.limit: Price is quote/calculator required for actual size and quantity. Vinyl, matte finish and durability are supplier claims; test intended surface and confirm whether turnaround includes transit.

sources.title: Flexible printed magnets
sources.summary: Described as ferrite/rubber/plastic sheet with a white vinyl face, about 0.38 mm / 15 mil. The supplier says there is no UV laminate and extended outdoor exposure may fade print.
sources.limit: Selected price, MOQ and delivery need confirmation. Supplier pull-strength claims do not establish product safety or applicable regulatory classification.

sources.title: Wood ornament production example
sources.summary: Zap Creatives lists 4 mm maple veneer ornaments up to 75 mm / three inches, with printed finishes and thread options. Publishes 7–9 working days after proof approval; assembly can add 1–2 days.
sources.limit: Shipping is separate; exact price/availability require confirmation. Buildworks proposes different dimensions, so this listing is a process example rather than a quote for Civic Canopy.

sources.title: Wood charms and single samples
sources.summary: Maple, cherry or walnut veneer wood charms, with single-unit samples and a published 7–9 working-day production window after proof approval. Natural grain varies.
sources.limit: Supplier-specific 4 mm veneer and tolerances need checking against artwork. Assembly may add 1–2 days; shipping, pricing and order acceptance remain unconfirmed.

sources.title: Standard paper-card price benchmark
sources.summary: MOO Original cards: 50 for US$23 ($0.46 each) or 100 for $45 ($0.45 each), on 16 pt / 130 lb stock. Standard trim 3.5 × 2 inches with matte/gloss options.
sources.limit: A card-printing benchmark, not custom backing-card manufacture. Holes, assembly, shipping and tax are separate; delivery depends on the calculator and chosen service.

sources.title: Small parts and intended audience
sources.summary: CPSC explains prohibited small parts in products intended for children under three, and warning requirements for certain toys/games for ages three through six. Design, marketing and recognized use matter to age classification.
sources.limit: A stated adult or 14+ label alone does not settle classification. Review the exact product, packaging, advertising and intended destination market before sale.

sources.title: Magnet requirements
sources.summary: CPSC describes scope and testing for magnet products, including loose or separable magnets. A decorative product name does not establish exemption. Magnet ingestion can cause serious injury.
sources.limit: Confirm scope under current 16 CFR 1262 or the applicable toy standard with a qualified reviewer. This page and our flexible-sheet concept do not certify compliance.

sources.title: Children’s product tracking labels
sources.summary: CPSC explains permanent legible tracking marks on products and packaging to the extent practicable: responsible manufacturer/private labeler, production location/date and batch/run details.
sources.limit: Apply the rules to the actual children’s product and any relevant exception. Keep batch records even when marking space is limited.

sources.title: Lead limits and material evidence
sources.summary: CPSC guidance describes the total-lead limit for accessible children’s-product components. Substrate, coating, ink and fastener need applicable evidence; an SDS alone does not establish compliance.
sources.limit: This guidance does not certify a supplier or our concepts. Coatings, electroplating and paint can have different testing rules; obtain product-specific reports and certificates as applicable.

sources.title: Paint and surface-coating guidance
sources.summary: CPSC explains lead-in-paint rules and distinctions among paints, printing and electroplating. Ask the maker to identify the coating and its applicable test scope.
sources.limit: Treatment differs by product/material. Do not infer safety or an exemption from the word enamel, water-based, plated or printed.

sources.title: Copyright and original expression
sources.summary: The US Copyright Office distinguishes original fixed expression from ideas. Keep written merchandising/reproduction permission for commissioned and third-party art, photos and fonts.
sources.limit: An original motif does not automatically clear all reference material or establish exclusive rights. No third-party artwork is licensed by this notebook.

sources.title: Trademark basics
sources.summary: USPTO explains trademarks as source identifiers. Check studio/collection names and conflicting marks before a commercial launch, and document any authorized brand use.
sources.limit: These original designs make no endorsement claim. This source does not establish that El Segundo Buildworks or its concept names have been cleared.

sources.title: Environmental claims and packaging
sources.summary: FTC guidance advises substantiating and qualifying environmental claims, including recyclability, recycled content and non-toxic claims. Specify whether a claim covers the product, its packaging or only a component.
sources.limit: The posted summary describes the 2012 Green Guides. Paper/wood content alone does not justify broad eco-friendly, recyclable or compostable promises; actual materials and local access matter.

provenance.creator: Original vector concept drawings authored for PointCast with Codex, 2026-10-03
provenance.method: Programmatically drawn SVG shapes; no stock photos, generated product photographs, copied logos, civic seals, Nouns artwork or commercial characters.
provenance.meaning: Colors, proportions, materials and dimensions express a design proposal. These drawings are not technical production files or evidence of manufactured goods.
provenance.rights: PointCast may use these commissioned original drawings for this project. Keep third-party fonts, supplier specifications and references under their own terms; make no exclusivity or trademark-clearance claim.
